1120834085205594113 [2019-04-23] @QiaochuYuan 💜 2
The emotional issues are suuuuper thorny. "Stop judging myself" is itself (potentially) a judgment, and there's a way of trying to force the stopping that is still self-violent in the same way that judgment is, and that doesn't work (in my experience). https://t.co/c78XNbrzki
  [Quoting @imhinesmi: @QiaochuYuan Do you have any advice for getting started with time tracking? I've tried doing it in the past but didn't manage to last more than 3 hours.  Though I suspect the answer is stop judging myself.]
↓
1120834086052827136 [2019-04-23] @QiaochuYuan 💜 2
Self-judgment is such a wild rabbit hole, lots to dig into here. Like the idea of an inner critic / inner authoritarian; part of you trying to keep the rest of you in line, in order to... be good? Be accepted? Can get real deep into parental / school / religious trauma here.
↓
1120834086749138944 [2019-04-23] @QiaochuYuan 💜 4 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
Instead of judgment, can try cultivating compassion + curiosity for yourself (much easier said than done, took me years to get anywhere): instead of "fuck, just spent the last 3 hours on reddit, I'm such a fuck up," more like "aww, poor baby, must be tired" kind of thing.

1334420343818162178 [2020-12-03] @RichDecibels 💜 15
I've sent 10K+ tweets so I get a lot of feedback about what the network wants. But my audience is still small enough that we are all weirdos.
↓
1334420345244225538 [2020-12-03] @RichDecibels 💜 22
Very large accounts are mostly not interesting at all. e.g. @naval is the archetype: with 1M followers he's producing the Hallmark-card version of insight. There's no joy, no eroticism, no rock'n'roll, no soul.
↓
1334420346620026881 [2020-12-03] @RichDecibels 💜 18
So maybe the feedback loop between me and the network has a sweet spot between popularity & weirdness. Enough popularity provides good training. but with too much popularity the feedback overwhelms the weird (ie. the novel, edgy, unexpected) in favour of the norm.
